links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT toothache responses (Flesch Reading Ease, FKGL, SMOG) versus websites
links.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 57.9 ± 3.2; Flesch-Kincaid 8.4 ± 0.6; SMOG 7.5 ± 0.4. ChatGPT had higher reading grade level than websites (ΔFKGL +0.4), though quality was higher (EQIP 85.3 ± 5.2).
links.quote: However, both ChatGPT and these conventional sources exhibit moderate readability, which may limit accessibility for individuals with low health literacy.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT's response quality and readability for common patient toothache queries compared to traditional websites, without evaluating specific deployment guardrails or practices.
